notes: Customer is highly latency-sensitive for user-facing chat. Primary disagreement to resolve: what metric counts for SLO enforcement. Velox insists on end-to-end client-side timings for UX guarantees (includes TLS handshake + network), while Redwood's initial SLA draft uses server-side processing time measured at the gateway. SE proposed hybrid approach: server-side processing time plus measured network tail allowances and a synthetic probe margin. Specific asks: (1) p95/p99 definitions tied to 'time-to-first-token' and 'time-to-last-token' separately, (2) explicit distinction between streaming and non-streaming endpoints in SLA, (3) instrumentation hooks for client SDKs to emit telemetry to Redwood console and to customer's Datadog/Sumo. Technical notes from 2/18 call: prefer server-reported 'queued->first-byte' and 'first-byte->stream-end' buckets; client will report 'request-sent->first-byte' for cross-checks. Proposed measurement plan for evaluation benchmark: run 72-hour dedicated-capacity test with realistic prompt distributions, KV-cache prewarm, mixed short/long-turn ratio (75% short, 25% long), measure p50/p95/p99 for TFt and TLa separately, and produce measurement alignment doc with example calculation snippets and instrumentation points. Negotiation stance: Velox will sign a 12-month reserved contract if Redwood accepts hybrid SLO language, provides Reserved GPU sizing cert, and includes credit table for p99 misses > 2% monthly.
